lines.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; as the 2026-11-15 rulings on this line. The zero for refunds of both spouses' 2024 tax on separate 2024 returns is the chosen reading of amb.2025.refund_two_returns (the worksheet tests one 2024 return; refused by refund.two_itemized_if_two on refund.taxable when both itemized with income taxes), and the cap at 2024 Schedule A line 5d is amb.2025.refund_cap_5d. Exceptions 1 and 5 (i1040gi p. 89, "1. You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024", "5. You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025") are refused by refund.not_prior_year on refund.taxable, the line Schedule 1 line 1 enters. Repeat disagreement; no value moves.

Ruling: representation; render UNCLEAR. The four helpers are defined lines rendered by label (refund.amt_you_born, amt_you_blind, amt_spouse_born, amt_spouse_blind: $1,550 or $1,950 per box checked), so line 6 is 'Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)'. The married-filing-separately condition of the worksheet footnote ('you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return', i1040gi p. 90) is in the spouse-box questions themselves (refund.spouse_born, refund.spouse_blind); a 2024 qualifying surviving spouse return has no spouse on it, so its spouse boxes are zero (refund.spouse_boxes; amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024).
